The Americans looked improved and composed in the second half after adjusting their high press. Spain did not produce a shot on target in the second half, and the US outshot them 13-6 on the day. Wilson thought she had scored the US’s first goal in the 53rd minute, but it was waved for offside after video review.

The US earned a penalty in the 67th minute after Wilson drew a foul by Natalia Ramos in the box. The taker was Yohannes – a surprise choice, given the 19-year-old has never attempted a penalty in four seasons at Ajax and OL Lyonnes. Wilson, a regular taker for the Portland Thorns, is a perfect 11 for 11 on penalties in the NWSL. (Yohannes told reporters after the game she was second on the US’s list of takers, behind Heaps.) Adriana Nanclares saved Yohannes’s stutter-step attempt and the Americans remained off the board.

Forward Mallory Swanson and midfielder Ashley Sanchez were among the second-half substitutes. Swanson, who was out for all of 2025 on maternity leave, made her first game appearance in 710 days. Sanchez was recalled to the national team amid a strong NWSL season with the North Carolina Courage and earned her first US minutes since October 2023. She nearly scored off a cross in the 88th minute but slid as her foot connected with the ball.
Spain increased the physicality for the final quarter-hour. They committed 12 fouls to the US’s four and went down to 10 players in stoppage time after Athenea del Castillo saw red for a hair pull.
The US will have a chance to remedy their finishing issues in Tuesday’s rematch in Pennsylvania. They have not gone consecutive games without scoring since the 2023 World Cup.
